text: As outlined in Introduction , many aspects of the placebo effect, especially outside the pain context, are yet unknown and would be worth investigating, preferably in an experimental study. Thus, the presented study has three goals: (1) the primary objective is to compare healthy adolescents with their parents regarding the experimentally induced placebo effect on mood and cognitive performance—measured via psychological questionnaires, reaction, and memory tests. It is hypothesized that placebo effects can be induced by an ineffective alleged Ginkgo transdermal patch, and that this effect is greater in adolescents than in adults. (2) Parents’ expectations about Ginkgo effects influence their children’s expectations and placebo effects and they, therefore, are correlated. (3) Finally, we will exploratively investigate whether this placebo application can decrease stress levels measured as psychophysiological responses such as HRV and skin conductance levels (SCL). We will also analyze if they differ between adolescents and parents.
source_label: Effects of Expectancy on Cognitive Performance, Mood, and Psychophysiology in Healthy Adolescents and Their Parents in an Experimental Study
